articles.title: Suspect who reportedly claimed to be LeBron James' son arrested for stalking at star's LA home, LAPD says
articles.summary: A man was arrested for felony stalking at LeBron James' Brentwood residence while the 76ers star was playing in Cleveland against the Cavaliers.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Police Department said Saturday that a man was arrested on Friday night at the Brentwood residence of LeBron James. James is in his first season with the Philadelphia 76ers after spending the previous eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers. James faced his former Cavaliers team in Cleveland on Friday. The Cavaliers selected him first overall in 2003, and he won a championship with them in 2016 during his second stint with the team. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE According to TMZ Sports, security spotted the suspect at roughly 9 p.m. and called 911. He was arrested on suspicion of stalking and later claimed he believed he was James’ son. The LAPD said to OutKick that the suspect was taken into custody without incident and was booked on charges of felony stalking. The suspect did not enter the home, TMZ said. KRISTAPS PORZINGIS STEPPING AWAY FROM BASKETBALL AMID HEALTH ISSUES: 'NOT WHERE I WANT TO BE' A spokesperson for James did not offer a comment. James struggled at his former home, scoring just eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, including 0-for-4 from three-point range. Cleveland won 119-95 as James' Sixers fell to 8-2 on the season. The NBA's all-time leading scorer is averaging 14.8 points, 7.4 assists, and 6.9 rebounds per game. articles.title: Duke's beatdown of NC State included a must-see missed field goal returned for a 109-yard touchdown
articles.summary: The Duke Blue Devils returned a missed NC State field goal 109 yards for a touchdown at Carter-Finley Stadium, turning a bad half into a nightmare.
articles.body: Not a whole lot has gone the NC State Wolfpack's way this season, and that was never more evident than after what the Duke Blue Devils did to them on Saturday afternoon in Raleigh. The Wolfpack welcomed their in-state rivals to Carter-Finley Stadium amid a rough season that saw them enter the game at 4-4, just weeks removed from a coaching change. Unfortunately, this one did not go their way, and the biggest bad bounce had to come at the very end of the first half, with NC State trailing 24-3. SUPER BOWL CHAMPION RUSSELL WILSON REPORTEDLY IN THE MIX FOR NC STATE HEAD-COACHING JOB Interim head coach Todd Goebbel sent out his kicking team with two seconds on the clock, hoping that kicker Kanoah Vinesett could at least hit a 50-yard field goal to end the half on a semi-high note. That did not happen. Vinesett didn't quite give it enough leg to get it the full 50 yards, and that worked out nicely for Duke as safety Andrew Pellicciotta was waiting in the end zone. He hauled in the kick and took off 109 yards for a touchdown. VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL That was so shocking; whoever was manning the CW's scorebug thought the kick was as good as gold and hung three points on the board. We don't see field goals returned for touchdowns nearly enough. It's easily one of the most exciting plays in football. The CFL got this right by having the goal posts at the front of the endzone (which also seems wildly unsafe, but at least they get more missed field goals returned for touchdowns). The only folks who didn't enjoy that, however, were NC State fans. That play flipped what should've been a 24-6 game at the half to one that was 31-3. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP And unfortunately, it didn’t get any better as the Blue Devils tacked on another 10 points to win this one, 41-3.

articles.title: Big Ten Network cuts to analyst Mike Locksley following Maryland’s win over Purdue
articles.summary: A little over two weeks ago, Mike Locksley stood on the Maryland Terrapins’ sidelines as their head football coach. On Saturday, he sat in the Big Ten Networ...
articles.body:
A little over two weeks ago, Mike Locksley stood on the Maryland Terrapins' sidelines as their head football coach.

On Saturday, he sat in the Big Ten Network studio watching them snap a 13-game Big Ten losing streak against the Purdue Boilermakers.

The Terps held on to defeat the Boilermakers 34-29 in West Lafayette, Indiana, and afterward interim head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim received a Gatorade bath and was carried off the field, creating a heartwarming scene.

That scene got a little awkward when BTN left the game and returned to its studio show, where Locksley, fired Oct. 21 after eight seasons , was asked to comment on the victory and celebration. The former coach was graceful, praising the team and Aazaar, and noting that he'd picked them to win the game beforehand.

"Congrats to Coach Aazaar and the Maryland Terrapin football team. It was a complimentary game," he said. "When you look in the first half, the way the defense did a great job of holding them to field goals, and then the offense comes out, four TDs in four straight drives to blow the game open and then win it at the end in a close game at the end."

Fellow BTN analyst Gerry DiNardo seemed to understand the uncomfortable nature of the moment, and took a moment to point out that quarterback Malik Washington, who passed for 253 yards and was responsible for four touchdowns, was Locksley's recruit.

"Malik Washington's not at Maryland if it wasn't for you," said DiNardo, patting his fellow analyst's arm.

articles.title: Billam-Smith stopped as Clarke repeats amateur win
articles.summary: Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith is knocked down and stopped for the first time in his professional career as Chev Clarke wins their no...
articles.body:
Former cruiserweight world champion Chris Billam-Smith was knocked down and stopped for the first time in his career as Chev Clarke won their all-British non-title fight on Saturday.

Londoner Clarke landed a big right hand at the start of the seventh round and although Billam-Smith beat the count, he was down again moments later after a barrage of punches.

The contest was allowed to continue but the Bournemouth fighter looked unsteady on his legs and when Clarke connected with two more blows, the referee stepped in.

Billam-Smith immediately protested against the decision, while Clarke stood in the middle of the ring shrugging his shoulders.

Clarke moves to 13 wins with two defeats and inflicts the third professional defeat for Billam-Smith who also lost to Gilberto Ramirez in 2024 and Richard Riakporhe in 2019.

"I do what champions do," said Clarke, who also beat Billam-Smith when they met in the amateur ranks a decade ago.

"I'm happy. Arsenal won and I won. My training camp was good and you saw that in the ring. I'll take all-comers going forward."

The likes of heavyweight Johnny Fisher, Traitors star King Kenny and strongman Eddie Hall were all spotted watching on from ringside in a Copper Box arena that was far from full, with just the lower tier of seats open for fans.

After a slow start to the contest with lots of holding, Clarke looked the sharper man as he landed some clean shots on the former world champion.

In the second round, the Londoner landed a big overhand right to the side of Billam-Smith's head. Clarke also connected in the third round with a big uppercut and an overhand right that snapped back Billam-Smith's head.

The former world champion, struggling to find his rhythm, was caught by another uppercut before Billam-Smith responded with a short right hook that made Clarke stumble back to his corner.

But in the seventh round Clarke broke Billam-Smith down, scoring two quick knockdowns before the referee intervened.

Fight promoter Dana White said after the fight that he felt the decision to stop the fight might have been a little premature.

Bentley beats bloodied Mosley Jr and calls out Benn

In the main support bout, Britain's Denzel Bentley beat a bloodied and brave Shane Mosley Jr, out-classing the American to win via a unanimous points decision.

Bentley scored a big knockdown in the second round, landing a straight right hand that made Mosley stagger backwards before following up with another right hand that dropped him to the canvas.

Mosley survived the count and the rest of the round but was routinely tagged by Bentley throughout the contest.

The Londonder landed sharp shots off the back foot and in the fifth round drew blood over the right eye of Mosley.

Bentley ended the fight strongly, boxing at times with his hands down and moving round his opponent as he landed eye-catching shots that attracted applause from the fans.

After 10 rounds the scorecards read 96-94 96-93 95-94 in Bentley's favour, with the 31-year-old then pointing at Conor Benn in the audience and suggesting a potential future match-up between the two.

Bentley was stripped of his WBO middleweight title in late October having agreed to fight Mosley instead of face his mandatory challenger.

His interim title was previously elevated to a full world championship belt following Janibek Alimkhanuly's decision to move up to super-middleweight.

articles.title: Bill Belichick reacts to Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots honor
articles.summary: Everything Bill Belichick said about the Patriots honoring Rob Gronkowkski.
articles.body:
EAST HARTFORD, Conn. — After his North Carolina team finished off its win at UConn in his first game back in New England, former Patriots coach Bill Belichick responded to events happening in Foxborough.

About 100 miles away at Gillette Stadium, Rob Gronkowski was being inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame.

"He played a tremendous role in who I am as a player. I really loved the way he challenged me," Gronkowski said. "He's the best football coach I've ever seen in my life, that I've ever been a part of as well. ... I thank him for that and I wouldn't be here without him."

Belichick, who won six Super Bowls in New England, has often steered clear of any Patriots-related discussion after being fired by the team.

But he made an exception for Gronkowski. Belichick smiled when told what Gronkowski said. He revealed that he'd reached out to his former star to congratulate him.

"That's nice of Rob to say that," he said during his postgame press conference. "I talked to Rob and congratulated him on his selection into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Well deserved. He was the best tight end in football during his time and one of the best of all time. I'm proud of Rob and what he's accomplished.

"He came a long, long way from barely playing in college at Arizona," Belichick continued, "to where he ended up, which was an incredible credit to him, his work ethic, his toughness and his dependability. It's a hard position to play, but he excelled at it. We wouldn't have won as many games as we did without him, I can tell you that. He's a big part of it. I love Rob."

articles.title: Dominant wins for Corning, Horseheads, TAE, Waverly in football semis
articles.summary: Corning, Horseheads, Waverly, and Thomas A. Edison secured spots in Section 4 football title games with decisive semifinal victories.
articles.body:
Corning, Horseheads, Waverly, and Thomas A. Edison were dominant in Section 4 football semifinal contests, earning spots in championship games next week.

Watkins Glen/Odessa-Montour fell short against defending state champion Tioga Central in a Class D semifinal.

A recap of Elmira-Corning region teams in sectional semifinals played Friday, Nov. 6 and Saturday, Nov. 7.

Hours after it was announced he was named the section's Class AA Player of the Year by the Section 4 Football Coaches Association , Corning's John Graham returned the opening kickoff 85 yards for a touchdown to set the tone in the Hawks' home semifinal triumph Friday night.

"When we're clicking on all three sides of the ball, we're pretty good and we're tough to beat," Corning head coach Mike Johnston Jr. said. "To open the game up with the kickoff return was huge. He shows why he's the Section 4 Class AA Player of the Year and continues to make big plays for us."

Graham added touchdown runs of 5 yards and 1 yard as Corning led 30-7 at halftime on the way to its second lopsided win this season against the Little Red. Corning, which began its combined program in 2010, has never lost to Ithaca.

Graham finished with 96 yards on 13 rushes on a night Corning had 10 players run the ball.

Fellow wingback Keegan Kelly added 86 yards on eight rushes to go with an interception on defense. Fullback Keegan VanCise carried 14 times for 78 yards, including a 1-yard touchdown.

Ashton Neally added two touchdowns for the Hawks, the first on a 19-yard reception of a Nate Bretch throw, and the second on a 4-yard run that put Corning up, 44-7, just over two minutes into the final quarter.

"It wasn't like somebody ran for 200 yards," Johnston said. "It was a collective effort by our team. A lot of the credit goes to our line. We were able to throw the ball tonight as well, and our defense was pretty solid as well. Just an all-around great effort by everybody."

Touchdowns for Ithaca (5-5) came on a 36-yard run from Jasmir Robbins in the first half, and a 29-yard strike from Leo Fiorello to Shy'von Williams late in the game.

Robbins rushed for 72 yards on eight carries. He sat out the second half after he was shaken up on the final play of the first half.

Corning responded after a 33-7 loss to Union-Endicott in last week's regular-season finale. Little went right for the Hawks in that game, including more than 200 penalty yards, a dropped touchdown, and some injuries that sidelined key players in the second half.

"I'd like to think that we turned the corner," Johnston said. "We've still got a ways to go with some guys, getting them healthy. I know Elmira gets the bye week and their kids will be back to full go."

Up next : Corning (6-4) will play Elmira (6-3) in the championship game at 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Elmira's Thomas J. Hurley Athletic Complex. Elmira topped Corning, 14-8, in the regular season and has beaten the Hawks in the last three Section 4 Class AA finals.

"This is the rivalry game that you play for all season," Johnston said. "Both of us have this date circled on the schedule, that we want to play each other in the sectional championship. That's our ultimate goal, to win the sectional championship."

Five players scored touchdowns Friday night as the Blue Raiders built a 41-0 halftime lead on the way to a home semifinal victory over the Patriots.

Jaxson Burchard had touchdown runs of 44 and 76 yards. He carried three times for 130 yards before leaving with an injury.

Bryce Thomas added 58 yards and a touchdown on five rushes, Sullivan Kraft contributed 132 yards and a TD on seven rushes, and Ben Peffer had 32 yards and a touchdown on three carries.

Horseheads quarterback Lyncoln Bennett connected with Jack Patchett for touchdowns of 4 and 24 yards.

Thomas led the defense with seven tackles. Patchett and Noah Gee had five tackles each, with Elijah Miller contributing four tackles.

Up next : Horseheads (8-2) will host Union-Endicott (7-3) in the championship game Friday, Nov. 13. Horseheads beat U-E, 21-15, during the regular season after falling to the Tigers, 21-20, in overtime in last year's sectional final .

U-E was a 35-0 winner over Vestal in Friday's other semifinal.

8-man: Thomas A. Edison 54, Unatego/Franklin/Unadilla Valley 27

Edison senior quarterback Jace Schiller accounted for seven touchdowns for the third time this season as the Spartans moved within one victory of the program's first Section 4 title with an eight-man semifinal victory at Ithaca High School.

Schiller completed 10-of-14 passes for 157 yards and two touchdowns. His contribution on the ground included 255 yards and five touchdowns on 40 carries.

On Friday, Schiller was named the Section 4 Football Coaches Association's eight-man Player of the Year.

Connor Lasko had four catches for 84 yards and a TD for Edison. Tanner Buchanan also caught a touchdown pass.

TAE's Paxton Hoover caught four passes for 52 yards, and he had five carries for 61 yards.

Edison's other touchdown came on a 12-yard run from Jimmy Haskins to make the score 54-14 early in the final quarter.

In Edison's 48-44 regular-season win over Unatego/Franklin/UV, Schiller passed for four touchdowns and ran for three. He opened the season by scoring seven touchdowns against Elmira Notre Dame in a game called at halftime.

Up next : Edison (7-1), the state's third-ranked eight-man team, will meet Lansing in the championship game at 5 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Chenango Valley. Edison was a 34-21 winner over Lansing during the regular season.

Class C: Waverly 41, Susquehanna Valley 12

Cooper Chrystie rushed for 141 yards and two touchdowns to go with 129 passing yards and a TD as Waverly downed Susquehanna Valley at home Friday in a Class C semifinal.

Bryce LaForest carried 10 times for 86 yards and a touchdown for Waverly.

Up next : Waverly (8-2) will face defending sectional champion Chenango Forks (10-0) in the title game at noon Saturday, Nov. 14 at Binghamton Alumni Stadium. Forks, ranked first in the state, was a 54-14 semifinal winner over Oneonta on Friday.

Class D: Tioga 12, Watkins Glen/Odessa-Montour 7

Tioga quarterback Jackson Bombard ran for two touchdowns in the final six minutes as the Tigers rallied to beat Watkins Glenn/Odessa-Montour in a Class D semifinal at Union-Endicott.

Bombard's 3-yard TD run brought the Tigers within 7-6 with 5 minutes, 25 seconds remaining. The try for two was no good. Tioga then recovered a high kickoff at Watkins Glen/Odessa-Montour's 34-yard line. Bombard scored on a 29-yard run with 3:49 to play for the game's final points.

The Storm's Mason Dupay broke a scoreless tie with a 4-yard TD run with just over nine minutes remaining. He finished with 56 yards on 12 rushes.

WG/O-M quarterback Hunter Mowry completed 10-of-14 passes for 103 yards. Kayden Garrabrant had three catches for 60 yards.

The Storm finished with a 7-3 record after posting the program's first playoff victory against Sidney, 49-6, in the quarterfinals.

Up next : Tioga (8-2) will play Delhi (9-1) in the sectional final at 8 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13 at Chenango Valley. Delhi opened the season with a 41-26 win over Tioga.

articles.title: Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil
articles.summary: Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil Credits: LUCAS UEBEL/GREMIO FBPAGrêmio drew 1–1 with Atlético-MG this Saturday (7) at Arena MRV in...
articles.body:
Grêmio are the first finalists of the 2026 Copa do Brasil Credits: LUCAS UEBEL/GREMIO FBPA

Grêmio drew 1–1 with Atlético-MG this Saturday (7) at Arena MRV in Belo Horizonte to reach the 2026 Copa do Brasil final. Having won the first leg 2–0 in Porto Alegre, the result in the Minas Gerais capital was enough to secure the team from Rio Grande do Sul a place in the final.

Atlético-MG, who needed to win by at least two goals to force a penalty shootout, pressed from the start and opened the scoring with a stunning long-range strike from left-back Renan Lodi in the 26th minute. Around ten minutes later, striker Carlos Vinicius equalized for Grêmio, who also benefited from an excellent performance by goalkeeper Weverton.

Grêmio will contest the Copa do Brasil final for the tenth time in their history and await the outcome of the tie between Vasco and Palmeiras, who meet this Sunday (8) at 5 p.m. (Brasília time) at São Januário in Rio. Palmeiras hold a 1–0 lead.

Whether they face Vasco or Palmeiras, the team from Rio Grande do Sul will be seeking their sixth title in the competition, which would put them level with Cruzeiro as the most successful club in Copa do Brasil history. They currently have five titles: 1989, 1994, 1997, 2001 and 2016. Reaching the final guarantees Grêmio at least a place in the preliminary rounds of the 2027 CONMEBOL Libertadores, the berth awarded to the runners-up. The champions will qualify for the group stage of the 2027 CONMEBOL Libertadores.

articles.title: Russell vents fury at Mercedes after missing out on pole in São Paulo
articles.summary: George Russell was again left furious with his Mercedes team after being pipped to pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris. Norris, deposed as worl...
articles.body:
George Russell was again left furious with his Mercedes team after being pipped to pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris.

Norris, deposed as world champion by Kimi Antonelli last weekend, conquered thunderstorms to clinch an impressive pole as the rain poured down.

Russell was facing a five-place grid penalty due to an engine change but was still determined to land pole as he and Norris slugged it out. But he was told to back off on his final flying lap before the rain worsened and his chance had gone.

"You told me to back off, what the hell?" Russell bellowed on the radio. Team principal Toto Wolff tried to calm his driver by saying: "George, you are p2."

That seemed to make matters worse, as Russell barked: "P2? I don't want to be P2, I want to be P1!"

It adds to a season of frustration for pre-season title favourite Russell, having had to watch 20-year-old team-mate Antonelli storm to the title while he says he had been undone by issues in 14 of the 20 weekends prior to this.

"Congrats to Lando but that was a pole lap and a misjudgement on our side," Russell said.

"For me personally, given the circumstances of last week, it would have meant a lot to me to take pole today.

"I missed it last week by nine milliseconds, but that was a real surprise. Today I really felt every lap I was doing was... I was at the top of the leaderboard most laps I completed.

"So yeah, I'm really disappointed with how that panned out. In the scheme of things, it doesn't change a huge amount."

Russell was asked about the message from Wolff but played down any frustration over it.

"When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," he added.

"You've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today. And there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently. So it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high.

"There's no point for pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally."

Wolff admitted in a video posted by Mercedes they may have made the wrong call with Russell behind Alex Albon on track, saying: "George was absolutely the quickest and should have been on pole. We are trying to do our best, I'm not sure we should have aborted the lap."

Russell will start seventh, one of a number of drivers hit by grid drops. Lewis Hamilton received a 10-place penalty but his new engine began smoking during practice and Ferrari ultimately had to change his entire power unit.

He will start from the back alongside Max Verstappen, while Charles Leclerc starts 14th after his 10-place drop.

Liam Lawson, whose Racing Bulls future remains in doubt, will start from a remarkable third - a place behind Antonelli - with Nico Hülkenberg, Isack Hadjar and Ollie Bearman ahead of Russell.

But it was Norris who showed his world champion class to sit proudly on top spot as he bids to join the battle for second in the championship.

"There are conditions where you feel like you can make a little bit more of a difference at times, for sure," Norris said.

"I'm against good guys who also have the capabilities to go for pole. And today we managed to do it because I put two good laps together.

"I think it's just a good thing for me to know that when I have that opportunity, I can make the most of it like today.

"When I have the three opportunities in the middle of the season to be on pole, to win races, we did every time."

articles.title: Clippers Have Multiple Potential Trade Candidates to Monitor This Season
articles.summary: The Clippers have multiple veterans who could be trade candidates in February.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers have had a tough start to their season. They have lost seven games in a row after beating the Sacramento Kings on opening night, and because of injuries, the season has spiraled downhill for them very fast.

Los Angeles has been without forward Brandon Ingram and guards Bradley Beal and Jordan Miller to start the season. They were also without Max Strus to start the year, but he recently came back from injury and has stepped in quickly.

The injuries have caused the Clippers to have some chemistry issues, as many of their young players have had the chance to get increased roles early in the season. Players like rookie guard Keaton Wagler have had a lot of reps so far this season, and with the direction they're heading in, the Clippers could want to see more out of those young pieces.

Even though Los Angeles has struggled as a team, they have individual players that can help out other teams contending for a championship, making them trade candidates come the deadline in February.

Players like Rui Hachimura, Brook Lopez , Darius Garland, and Kris Dunn have all had their ups and downs this season, but they're established veterans who can surely help winning teams at the moment.

The first player who could draw interest from other teams is center Brook Lopez. Lopez has averaged 13.5 points per game and 5.1 rebounds, and he's had games where he's arguably been the Clippers' best offensive weapon.

He's also known to be one of the better shooting big men in the NBA, and so far, he's shot 42.3 percent from three-point range, making him one of the top shooters on the team.

Another player that the Clippers could consider dealing is guard Kris Dunn. Like Lopez, Dunn has had big individual games for Los Angeles this season, and he's known to be a solid two-way guard that a contending team could use off the bench.

So far this season, Kris Dunn is averaging 8.5 points per game, and defensively, he's averaging 2.8 steals. He's capable of having offensive outbursts as well. Against the Oklahoma City Thunder, he led the way with 15 points on 6-of-7 shooting from the field.

Los Angeles still has a chance to turn things around this season as players slowly start to come back from injury, but if the losing persists, the Clippers may have to move off some veterans because of the lack of future draft picks and the value some of their players have right now.

articles.title: Cincinnati receiver JV Gibson carted off after taking hard hit in game vs. UH
articles.summary: JV Gibson was down on the field for several minutes before leaving on a stretcher after taking a hard hit near the goal line.
articles.body:
Cincinnati wide receiver JV Gibson was taken off the field on a stretcher after taking a hard hit near the goal line late in the fourth quarter Saturday against Houston .

Gibson attempted to make a catch near the goal line when he was hit by Houston safety Jordan Allen with 6:59 left in the game and the Bearcats in position to tie the game.

Gibson remained on the field for several minutes as the entire Cincinnati team kneeled nearby. A family member gave a thumbs up as the cart left the field.

Allen was called for targeting and ejected from game.

articles.body:
ASHEVILLE, N.C. (AP) — Jaxon Prunty had 19 points in Western Carolina's 83-75 win against UNC Asheville on Saturday.

Prunty shot 3 of 12 from the field, including 3 for 9 from 3-point range, and went 10 for 11 from the line for the Catamounts (1-1). Jaeden Roberts scored 17 points, shooting 5 for 9 (2 for 5 from 3-point range) and 5 of 6 from the free-throw line. Malachi Brown had 16 points and shot 4 of 7 from the field, including 2 for 4 from 3-point range, and went 6 for 8 from the line.

Connor Dubsky finished with 16 points and three steals for the Bulldogs (1-2). UNC Asheville also got 15 points and eight rebounds from Ja'Corey Lipkins. Jermaurhiyun Anderson finished with 13 points.

articles.title: F1 São Paulo Grand Prix starting grid
articles.summary: How will the grid line up for the F1 São Paulo Grand Prix?
articles.body:
A chaotic qualifying session in wet conditions, coupled with a host of power unit penalties, have resulted in an unexpected starting grid for Sunday's Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix.

Lando Norris took pole position , delivering the lap he needed at the start of Q3 before heavy rain saw the ten remaining drivers in the final segment of qualifying climb out of their cars before the clock struck zero. While George Russell took second, a five-place grid penalty will drop him to seventh, promoting teammate — and new F1 Drivers' Champion — Kimi Antonelli to P2.

The shocks truly begin on the second row, where Liam Lawson will start third for Visa Cash App Racing Bulls while Nico Hülkenberg will come off the line fourth for Audi. Isack Hadjar and Oliver Bearman will start fifth and sixth, respectively, while Fernando Alonso will start eighth next to Russell, in a. strong performance for the Aston Martin veteran.

Russell is not the only driver taking a grid drop for Sunday's race, which is expected to be run in wet conditions. Charles Leclerc will start down in P14 after taking a ten-place grid penalty, while teammate Lewis Hamilton will start in P20, after taking what goes into the books as a 75-place grid penalty.

Max Verstappen will start down in P21, after taking a 30-place grid penalty, while Sergio Pérez will round out the field in P22, thanks to a 30-place grid penalty of his own. Verstappen has charged back through the field at each of the last two races in Interlagos, winning in wet conditions at the 2024 installment despite starting in P17, and finishing third a year ago despite starting from pit lane.

With both Antonelli and Russell starting inside the top ten — and the Ferrari duo starting outside of the points — Mercedes is in a strong position to clinch the Constructors' Championship in this race .

articles.title: UCF football rallies past Kansas after two controversial catch reviews
articles.summary: The UCF Knights blew a 26-7 lead to Kansas in the second half, but snapped their 12-game road losing streak in dramatic fashion.
articles.body:
Two reviewed end-zone receptions ultimately decided the fate of UCF 's road losing streak Nov. 7 — one which did not go its way and one which certainly did.

From Kansas ' 15-yard line with 12 seconds remaining, Knights quarterback Alonza Barnett III lofted a pass toward the back left pylon which Waden Charles juggled and appeared to secure for the go-ahead touchdown. However, upon further review, he did not possess the ball before his backside touched out of bounds.

Two plays later, Barnett fired a strike toward the front left pylon that redshirt freshman Caden Piening corralled on what appeared to be the final play of regulation. The Big 12 Conference's replay operations center conferred with the on-field referee and chose to uphold the call on the field of touchdown.

UCF celebrated a 33-32 victory over Kansas after surrendering a 19-point, second-half lead. The Knights (5-4, 3-3 Big 12) prevailed away from the Bounce House for the first time since Sept. 14, 2024.

Barnett, making his first start since Sept. 12, completed 18 of 31 attempts for 251 yards with two touchdowns and one interception — UCF's opening play from scrimmage that set up Isaiah Marshall's 1-yard TD sneak to start the scoring. He added 36 rushing yards despite Kansas recording four sacks, in addition to 11 tackles for loss.

UCF can achieve bowl eligibility for the first time since 2023 with at least one win in any of their final three games. It will host Arizona State next weekend, following by a short turnaround and home date with Iowa State on Nov. 20 and a final trip to Colorado for Thanksgiving weekend.

articles.title: Nebraska fires offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen
articles.summary: Nebraska football made the move to fire offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen on Saturday afternoon.
articles.body:
Nebraska football fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen Saturday morning. Matt Rhule announced the move.

The firing comes following the Huskers' 24-13 loss to Illinois on Friday night. He is coming off a trend where the program failed to score more than 17 points in any game since the Indiana contest on October 10.

Before the Indiana game, Nebraska's offense scored 43.6 points per game and averaged 475.6 total yards per game. Following the matchup against the Hoosiers, the offense averaged just 13.5 points per game over the next four games.

"Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season," Rhule said in a statement. "As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program—including wins and losses—and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted. While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working. Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties. As I have recently shared, Dana has a fantastic offensive mind, he is a strong leader, and he has done great work here at Nebraska. But simply, we need a change. Co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas will take over play-calling duties."

Holgorsen joined Rhule's staff as an offensive consultant in November 2024. He succeeded Marcus Satterfield as offensive coordinator at the time. Now, the Huskers will look to find an offensive identity over the next couple of weeks.

It will be interesting to see if this is the first domino to fall on this coaching staff. It's clear the Huskers want to turn the page offensively. The program enters a crucial three-game stretch as it looks to finish the 2026 season on a high note.

articles.title: All-Ohio honors come home to area runners at OHSAA state cross country
articles.summary: The fourth time is a charm for Shelby’s Anna Will. It was back-to-back for Lexington's Gabi Twedt.
articles.body:
OBETZ — The fourth time is a charm for Shelby's Anna Will.

After qualifying for the state cross country championships in each of the last three seasons, but coming up short in her quest for an All-Ohio honor, the senior accomplished the elusive goal when she finished 33 rd with a 19:29.2 to take second team All-Ohio honors.

"I am really happy about it," Will said. "Every year, I have come here with the goal of earning All-Ohio and I have never got it. Finally getting it my senior year and my last race in a Shelby jersey is thrilling and means so much to me. It is something I have been working for since I was a freshman."

Last week at the regional meet, Will got boxed in and while she still earned an individual qualifying spot, she felt like she was held back from running her absolute best. So, she changed her strategy at Saturday's Ohio High School Athletic Association State Cross Country Championships and sprinted off of the line to get ahead of the pack. It worked well for her as she built a big enough advantage to withstand some late kicks from fellow runners to secure an All-Ohio spot.

"It was definitely a tough race because you pretty much have to sprint right out of the gate," Will said. "I am the kind of racer who would rather get out in a good spot and fall back a little bit rather than sit back and try to move up later. Knowing I had to go out faster was the right move because it put me in a better spot."

As a freshman, Will was 71 st with a 20:07.3 before taking 48 th with a 19:10.39 as a sophomore and 59 th with a 19:32.04 last season. She finally broke through as a senior and will join the All-Ohio honors at Shelby High School.

"It is all thanks to my teammates and coaches," Will said. "I would not be here without their support and encouragement. When I fell short, I had several people there picking me back up. And I credit it to God. Every day, I wake up with the ability to run and I am so thankful for being given that ability and I am going to use it to glorify him."

Lexington's Gabi Twedt becomes two-time All-Ohioan

Lexington sophomore Gabi Twedt made it two-for-two in trips to the state championships and bringing home All-Ohio honors.

Twedt took 18 th overall with an 18:46.4 to earn a spot on the first team All-Ohio podium. She was 20 th last year with an 18:47.18 so she continued to improve while putting herself in position to be a four-time All-Ohioan by the time her career is over.

"It is really special," Twedt said. "Today didn't go as well as I had hoped; I was hoping for a faster time, but with the conditions and how fast we had to get out in the first 400 meters, I will take it. I gave it my absolute best today."

Battling the blustery cold, Twedt managed to stay warm on her run. She was sitting at the 4:15.8 mark a mile in as she set a solid pace for the day.

"In warmups, we were prepared for it to be even colder than what it was and we were layered up," Twedt said. "But once we got running, we realized it was pretty perfect running weather and we prefer this over really hot races."

Lady Lex took 16 th as a team with 346 points as senior Jenna Halfhill was 52 nd with a 19:18.0, senior Evalynn Adkins was 95 th with a 19:54.4, junior Adira Sharrock was 165 th with a 20:39.4 and freshman Nyra Loy was 168 th with a 20:39.4 to round out the Top 5 scoring runners. Freshman Brynlee Brokaw was 196 th with a 21:24.5 and sophomore Alexis Neal was 200 th with a 21:40.2 to round out the runners for Lex.

While it was a disappointing team finish, Lady Lex had a lot to be proud of this season after winning an Ohio Cardinal Conference championship and taking runner-up honors at the regional championships, all after losing three runners from last year's team that placed third in the state.

"We knew going into the season it wouldn't match last year with all of the talent we lost," Twedt said. "But going from where we were at the start of the season to where we are now is a huge jump in improvement. I am so proud of my teammates. Last week was the best we have performed all season and even though we weren't amazing today, I know each one of them brought it and gave it their best and that is really all that matters."

And Twedt vows to continue to bring it during the offseason as she gets set to try to become a three-time All-Ohioan next season.

"It's all about continuing to train," Twedt said. "I do not want to hit the junior slump that is prevalent in cross country, so I am going to do my best to keep training and be ready for track and next season."

Hicks, Strim, Rhein earn All-Ohio honors in Division IV boys race

New London junior Carter Hicks was the top area finisher in the Division IV boys race as he took 24 th with a 16:21.1 while Colonel Crawford's Isaac Stirm was 34 th with a 16:34.6 as both runners nabbed All-Ohio honors. Crestline's Colten Keller was 82 nd with a 17:09.8 and Crestview's Isaac McFarland was 88 th with a 17:12.6 to round out the individual performances.

Black River took 18 th as a team with 466 points. Senior Connor Rhein earned All-Ohio honors by taking 27 th with a 16:30.6 while freshman Jackson Quallish was 141 st with a 17:47.0, sophomore Archer Combs was 145th with a 17:53.5, sophomore Ray Brakefield was 153 rd with a 17:59.8 and Brock Martin took 204 th with a 19:36.8 to round out the Top 5 runners for the Pirates. Freshman Leland Gallatin was 206 th with a 19:45.7 and senior Logan Rhein was 212 th with a 21:40.6.

Crestline girls post strong showing in first state meet in program history; Smith runs well for Hillsdale in Division IV girls race

The Crestline girls cross country team made the first state championship meet appearance in program history on Saturday and took 21 st with 459 team points. Senior Nevaeh Hill was 54 th with a 19:44.3 while senior Addison Hill was 125 th with a 20:57.7, senior Jocelyn Noblit was 154 th with a 21:36.0, sophomore Lillian Mills was 161 st with a 21:53.0 and Addysen Giesige was 176 th with a 22:12.7 to round out the top 5 runners. Sophomore Anna Erwin was 195 th with a 23:25.6 and sophomore Faith Songer was 197 th with a 23:33.7 to round out the runners for Crestline.

Hillsdale's Kloe Smith took 79 th with a 20:10.9 to end her junior season on a high note at state.

articles.title: Nets' Egor Demin (right leg bone bruise) won't play this weekend
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin will not play this weekend as he continues to recover from his right leg bone bruise, per head coach Jordi Fernandez.
articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin has missed the past four games as he continues to recover from a right leg bone bruise that he suffered in a 125-124 overtime loss to the Boston Celtics. Brooklyn put out a statement on Oct. 29 that Demin would be reevaluated in one week, meaning that he had a chance to play on Saturday against the Atlanta Hawks, but the plan has shifted.

"He's progressing well. He's on the court. He's not going to play today or tomorrow, and then we'll go from there," Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez said prior to Saturday's matchup against the Hawks, per Brian Lewis of the New York Post. While it's good news that Demin is progressing well in his recovery, him being unavailable on Saturday in Atlanta or Sunday at the Dallas Mavericks weakens Brooklyn's rotation.

Demin, 20 , is averaging 7.8 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game while shooting 31.0% from the field and 28.6% from behind the three-point line. With Demin out of the rotation for the time being, Fernandez has been experimenting with the rotation, including starting forward Danny Wolf against the Hawks with the usual starters in Nolan Traore, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, and Day'Ron Sharpe.

The Nets (2-6) begin their four-game road trip at Atlanta and that will be Brooklyn's second chance to notch a two-game winning streak, especially with the Hawks playing on the second night of a back-to-back. After Sunday's matchup at the Mavericks, the Nets' next game will be a visit to Zion Williamson and the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday so it's possible that Demin is back for that matchup.

Ultimately, this is an 82-game season and the Nets have always maintained the position of being patient with all of the players when it comes to injuries and Demin is the latest example. Brooklyn has the chance of winning a second-straight game in a row and while the former BYU Cougar won't be part of that equation, players like Porter and Randle will continued to do their part to lead this team.

Luke Fahey split reps as a high school quarterback until his senior year

At Mission Viejo, Fahey played in a two-quarterback system with Draiden Trudeau for his sophomore and junior seasons. Trudeau ended up as a three-star recruit in the Class of 2025 and committed to play football at San Diego State.

"I feel God has a plan for everybody," Fahey told the Los Angeles Times ahead of his senior season in 2025. "That was my journey. Of course, everyone wants to be a full-time starter, but that was a good thing for me. There was a lot of adversity during those two years."

articles.title: Ohio State’s implosion vs. Oregon reaches new low not seen in 27 years
articles.summary: Coach Ryan Day’s Ohio State Buckeyes had a strong first quarter at the Horsehoe in Columbus vs. the Oregon Ducks, but gave up 17 points in the second quarter...
articles.body:
Coach Ryan Day's Ohio State Buckeyes had a strong first quarter at the Horsehoe in Columbus vs. the Oregon Ducks, but gave up 17 points in the second quarter on a day when Luke Fahey filled in for injured QB Julian Sayin . The Buckeyes got a big prediction from a former All-American before the game, but let him down as they fell behind, 38-14, with four minutes left in the fourth and final quarter.

Stewart Mandel of The Athletic shared the news of Ohio State's epic collapse against the Ducks.

"Ohio State hasn't given up this many points at home to a team ranked this low since 1999," Mandel wrote.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The game also marked the first time the Buckeyes had given up 38 unanswered points since 1999 against the Wisconsin Badgers, as defensive coordinator Matt Patricia's unit was outfoxed and outplayed at Ohio Stadium.

The Buckeyes made the score a more respectable 38-22 after Luke Fahey rushed for a two-point conversion on the heels of a 13-yard touchdown toss to Jeremiah Smith . A strong rushing day from Bo Jackson did little to assuage frustrations of the Buckeyes' fans.

Ducks fans eagerly awaited the end of the game as they wondered how the postgame handshake would go between Lanning and Day after Day's viral dust-up with Lincoln Riley in Week 9 after losing to the USC Trojans.

The Ducks reeled off 5.6 yards per play while Ohio State had 4.9 yards per play and the game began to wind down in Columbus. Ohio State clung to faint hopes of a comeback victory, but Lanning and Oregon looked like they were about to secure a much-needed win over their nemeses and fellow Big Ten adervsaries.

articles.title: Grading Jared Curtis in Vanderbilt football win over Mississippi State
articles.summary: Vanderbilt football QB Jared Curtis did not have a touchdown or interception, but did have a fumble that resulted in a TD for Mississippi State.
articles.body:
STARKVILLE, MS − Jared Curtis got his first SEC win as a starter as Vanderbilt football took down Mississippi State 25-23 on Nov. 7 at Davis-Wade Stadium.

The Commodores (4-5, 1-5) got their first conference win thanks primarily to Brock Taylor's six field goals. The offense controlled the time of possession, holding the ball for nearly 40 minutes of game time.

Curtis didn't play his best or most flashy game of the season, but he operated the offense effectively and gave his team a chance to get a much-needed win.

Curtis was 17-for-27 for 168 yards passing. He didn't have any touchdowns or interceptions.

He ran 10 times for 35 yards, not including sacks. He was sacked three times for 13 yards, including one that resulted in a fumble returned for a touchdown by Mississippi State.

Jared Curtis performance vs Mississippi State

Curtis missed many of the downfield throws he usually makes. But he was still generally efficient, keeping things moving even though many of the drives stalled out in field goal range.

He did make one really bad play, fumbling on a sack that turned into a scoop-and-score touchdown for Mississippi State in the third quarter. Luckily for Curtis, the play happened early enough in the game that he was able to rebound.

Had Curtis hit more of his throws, he would've put the game out of reach. But he ultimately did enough for the victory.

articles.title: FSU snaps 1,078-day road drought with win at Boston College
articles.summary: Freshman Amari Thomas scored his first two career touchdowns, including the go-ahead run with 2:29 left. Next up for FSU: Pittsburgh.
articles.body:
Following the firing of Mike Norvell last week, Florida State football traveled to take on the Boston College Eagles for its first test under interim head coach Rick Stockstill on Saturday, Nov. 7. The Seminoles defeated the Eagles 31-24, ending a 1,078-day drought that hung over their heads.

FSU, which had not won a true road game since beating the University of Florida on Nov. 25, 2023, snapped a 12-game road losing streak against a team it had beaten in five of their previous six meetings. The lone loss came in 2024, the last time the two programs met, when the 'Noles fell at home, adding an extra layer to the feat.

"I dreamt all my life of, you know, one day being a coach at Florida State and to have this opportunity and to have a win, it's something that I'll cherish, you know, all my life," Stockstill said with tears in his eyes in the press conference after the game.

The matchup also served as a test of depth for the Garnet and Gold, as several key players are now sidelined with injuries. Two of Florida State's main offensive weapons, sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah and senior wide receiver Duce Robinson , are out for the season. The injury trend continued in the second quarter, when senior center Bradyn Welch-Joiner was carted off the field with a leg injury.

Daniels leads FSU second-quarter turnaround

The Garnet and Gold got off to a slow start in the first quarter, with senior quarterback Ashton Daniels completing none of his three pass attempts as the offense struggled to convert on third downs. Boston College jumped out to a 10-0 lead.

Florida State turned momentum around in the opening minutes of the second quarter when Daniels showcased his speed with a 4-yard rushing touchdown. Daniels finished the game completing 15 of 26 pass attempts, helping move the Seminoles down the field and allowing the offense to consistently respond.

FSU's theme of the game was to find a way. Fifth-year senior kicker Gabe Panikowski scored on a 1-yard run off a fake field goal with 51 seconds left in the first half. He then made the extra point to give FSU a 21-17 lead.

"I've been working on it for a little while now and I trust myself to run," Panikowski said in the press conference after the game. "I ran track and field in high school and I've actually always wanted to showcase my speed so I made sure that the coaches knew we had that in our toolbox."

The play showed that the 'Noles, despite being shorthanded on personnel due to injuries, can still find production from unexpected sources.

"I've got coach Bowden's blood in me," Stockstill said. "And you know he'd run a trick play too so maybe he's smiling down on me right now."

Thomas, Lopez fill roles amid offensive injuries

Freshman running back Amari Thomas scored his first career touchdown on a 20-yard run in the second quarter, stepping into the backfield in Kromah's absence. Thomas found the end zone again with 2:29 left in the game, scoring the go-ahead touchdown on FSU's game-winning drive.

"[Injuries are] adversity, every team faces it," Thomas said in the press conference after the game. "You just got to know what to do next, like when the moment comes, step up to the challenge and execute."

Fellow freshman wide receiver Jasen Lopez also rose to the occasion for the Garnet and Gold, notching four receptions for 54 yards, an average of 13.5 yards per catch.

"He's getting better every week," Stockstill said. "With Duce going down he got a little bit more of an opportunity there today and made some really nice plays."

Florida State now moves to 4-5 on the season and will look to continue its road success when the team travels to face the University of Pittsburgh at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13.

Gia Ciaccio is a Staff Writer for the FSView & Florida Flambeau, the student-run, independent online news service for the FSU community. Email our staff at contact@fsview.com.

articles.title: Oklahoma State football scores monster win vs K-State behind Caleb Hawkins | Report card
articles.summary: The Oklahoma State football bounceback against K-State was powered by Caleb Hawkins and the offense. Here's our grades from the Cowboys' 66-28 rout of the Wi...
articles.body:
MANHATTAN, KS — Oklahoma State football needed a bounce back after last week's disappointment at Iowa State.

The woeful Wildcats were no match for the Cowboys , offensively or defensively. OSU rolled up 49 points in the first half alone, the most any Cowboy team has scored in a half since a 49-point explosion at Texas Tech in 2011.

Oklahoma State Cowboys vs Kansas State Wildcats in Week 10 college football, see photos

Hawkins finished with 246 total yards and four touchdowns. On the ground, he had 175 yards and three touchdowns on 20 carries and added 71 receiving yards and one touchdown on six catches.

He did most of his damage before halftime when the Cowboys built a huge lead. He had 159 yards rushing and three rushing touchdowns on only 17 carries in the first half.

That was never more evident than with his first touchdown of the day, a 21-yard scamper punctuated by him lunging and stretching the ball toward the goal line. Initially, he was ruled short, but after review, Hawkins kept his body off the ground, using the defender who was tackling him to avoid putting down a knee or elbow.

If not for a pick-six, the Cowboy quarterback would've had a nearly perfect day.

He was 22 of 28 for 313 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. That pick was returned for a K-State touchdown, and it came at a time the Wildcats were already down three touchdowns and searching for answers.

Mestemaker and Co. more than bounced back from it, but an interception-free day would've been ideal.

Still, Mestemaker was superb. It was his eighth consecutive game with at least 300 yards passing, a program record.

Mestemaker didn't throw his first incompletion until almost five minutes into the second quarter, and he completed almost 80% of his passes.

The Cowboy secondary was not perfect. The Wildcats' first touchdown, for instance, was a 73-yard pass to a wide-open receiver who simply ran by the cornerbacks and went by the safeties without so much as a glance.

But the secondary also had three interceptions, two by LaDainian Fields and one by Quinton Hammonds.

Fields now leads the country with seven picks this season, and he has six in the past four games. His seven interceptions through the first nine games of the season is the most for a Cowboy since Darrent Williams in 2003.

If the secondary can be more boom than bust, it's good news for the Cowboys.

The Cowboy defense was credited with one sack, seven quarterback hurries and three tackles for loss.

Still, the OSU defense was in the backfield a lot more than those numbers indicate.

Early in the second quarter, for instance, the Cowboys brought a safety blitz around the edge, and even though Evan Jackson didn't get home for the sack, he disrupted the timing of the play. The result was a running play that didn't go anywhere.

Getting into the backfield made life difficult on K-State quarterback Blake Barnett, who made his first career start on Saturday. He gave way to Dillon Duff after halftime after being roughed up in the first half.

Up 56-21, the Cowboys ran a trick play for a touchdown late in the third quarter.

OSU coach Eric Morris said after the game that he felt like another touchdown at that point was a good idea. But it sure felt like the Wildcats could've played another four quarters and not gotten to 56 points, so it wasn't the greatest look for Morris and his Cowboys.

Now, the play was super cool. Terrence Lewis got the handoff and ran left, then pitched the ball to Wyatt Young who was headed right. After Young took a few steps, the receiver stopped and floated the ball to a wide-open Drew Mestemaker.

It was the Cowboy quarterback's first career catch and first career receiving touchdown.

But going to the bag of tricks to go ahead 63-21? It feels like rubbing it in, but even worse, it wastes a fantastic trick play that could've been used, oh, I dunno, next week against Texas Tech.

OSU cornerback LaDainian Fields and K-State tailback Rodney Fields had only ever been on a football field as teammates before Saturday.

The cousins faced off for the first time, and while LaDainian got the best of the matchup, both on the scoreboard and on the stat sheet, both had successful moments. LaDainian had two interceptions in addition to three tackles and one quarterback hurry while Rodney finished with 87 yards and one touchdown on 20 carries.

They even went head-to-head a couple of times.

The first time came late in the first quarter when LaDainian tracked down Rodney and tackled him along the sideline for an 8-yard gain. LaDainian pulled Rodney off the ground and gave him a super quick pat on the back.

Cowboy coach Eric Morris knows the impact Wildcat fans can have in Manhattan.

He recalled playing games at K-State when they've been bonkers.

But Saturday, his Cowboys not only kept the fans under control but sent a lot of them home early. The Wildcat fans cleared out in droves at halftime, and the exodus only continued as the game progressed.

OSU's early control of the game was huge. K-State won the coin toss and opted to take the ball instead of deferring to the second half. Morris said defensive players were fired up on the sidelines at what felt like an affront, but then, they went out and did something about it, getting a three-and-out.

Three plays later, the OSU offense was in the end zone, the rout was on and the crowd was never a factor.

K-State doesn't have a very good football team, but it provided a perfect day for football.

There might been better days for a college football game, but maybe not.

articles.title: Runnin' Rebels improve to 2-0 with gutsy win over Samford
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS – Runnin’ Rebels head coach Josh Pastner says that his team’s biggest strength is that their go-to man is the open man.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS – Runnin' Rebels head coach Josh Pastner says that his team's biggest strength is that their go-to man is the open man.

That claim rang true in UNLV's 88-79 victory over Samford at Thomas & Mack Center on Saturday.

Five Rebels scored in double figures as UNLV improved to 2-0 — underpinning their selfless mindset to start the campaign.

Sophomore Cam Miles led the way this time with 20 points — shooting 4-for-9 from three-point range and 8-for-8 from the free-throw line. Tyrin Jones made winning plays in bunches, chipping in 17 points, five rebounds, six blocks, and two steals. He drew praise from Pastner for knocking down seven of his 10 attempts at the charity stripe.

Elsewhere, last game's hero Sebastian Mack poured in 17 points on 7-for-13 shooting. He didn't have to erupt today because this Rebels team is constructed to play together.

It just so happened to be Miles' turn to set a new scoring career high.

"I have to give it all to my teammates," Miles said afterward. "As soon as I came in, they welcomed me in as a brother. The chemistry that we have is amazing. They give me confidence and energy. They're always talking to me, making sure I'm up."

Miles oozed confidence as he buried a 28-foot triple with 1:25 remaining in the second half, all but putting the visitors away at 88-78.

Jones made his presence felt on both ends of the floor as the Rebels struggled to find separation from the pesky Bulldogs, who hung around tough.

UNLV finally created some daylight between the two teams late. Jones grabbed an offensive board and kicked the ball out to Miles for a three-pointer before converting a couple of free throws and finishing strong at the basket on the following play with the shot clock dwindling. That made it 85-78 — tying the hosts' largest lead of the game — with 3:06 left to play.

Pastner was in great spirits entering the media room postgame. He's pleased with the work his team has put in their first two games.

"I think both teams we played this week are good teams," he said. "There is so much parity amongst college basketball now."

Pastner shared that his three keys to the victory were: adhering to the game plan by guarding the three-point line — with Samford being a shooting team, free throws, and offensive rebounding.

The Rebels held the visitors to just 5-for-20 from beyond the arc. 20 of the Bulldogs' 62 field goal attempts came from deep, when usually they take about half of their shots from the outside, according to Pastner.

UNLV made 25 of 32 free throws, limiting Samford to just 19 attempts (14 makes) with disciplined defense.

The hosts out-rebounded the Bulldogs 38-28, with the 11 offensive boards providing a decisive edge.

The Rebels are feeling really good about their start to the year. They are a talent-packed team that's already had to demonstrate some grit against a couple of teams that simply refused to get blown out.

The hope is that this group has come out of these wins better than they were before. The biggest test to date awaits them next, however, as the Rebs will host Stanford (2-0) on Friday.

MIAMI (AP) — Devonte Lyons ran for a career-high 216 yards and two touchdowns, and Robert Czeremcha kicked a 42-yard field goal late in the game to give Florida International a 20-17 victory over Missouri State on Saturday night.

Lyons scored on a 17-yard run early in the fourth quarter that stretched the FIU lead to 17-6. After a Yousef Obeid 22-yard field goal for Missouri State, J.J. O'Neal forced a fumble near midfield and Jashawn Cooper returned the ball into the end zone for the Bears that tied the game at 17-all with 6:42 left to play.

Czeremcha kicked the game-winner with 1:55 remaining, capping a 10-play, 54-yard drive. Henry Belin IV drove the Bears to the FIU 22 with 21 seconds left, but was called for intentional grounding on third down to end it.

Lyons had 24 carries that included a 56-yard run and a short-yardage score.

JJ Kohl threw for 183 yards and an interception for FlU (4-5, 2-3 Conference USA), which ended a three-game skid.

Belin threw for 225 yards for Missouri State (3-6, 2-2).

articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith 's Heisman Trophy bid is likely lost with the Buckeyes picking up their third loss of the season .

The Buckeyes were stunned by the Ducks in a 41-28 beatdown on Nov. 7, losing their third game of the regular season for the first time in 15 years. Ohio State led 14-0 at the end of the first quarter, then surrendered 38 straight points.

A majority of Smith's production came after the Buckeyes trailed by multiple scores late in the fourth quarter. Smith caught a 13-yard touchdown pass with 3:25 remaining.

OSU wide receiver Jeremiah Smith in action: Photos from 2026 Ohio State football season

What are Jeremiah Smith's odds to win the Heisman Trophy?

Smith has +700 odds to win the Heisman Trophy, according to BetMGM on Nov. 7 at 8:06 p.m.

Smith had +275 odds to win the award before Ohio State's loss to Oregon. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, who plays against Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr on Nov. 7, leads all Heisman odds at +110

Buckeyes face Oregon in college football matchup. See the photos

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith stats vs Oregon

Smith had seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown against Oregon.

Smith has 69 receptions for 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns in the 2026 season.

Smith has 232 receptions, 3,758 yards and 41 touchdowns in his career.

Where will Jeremiah Smith end up in the 2027 NFL Draft?

Smith acknowledged before the season began that the 2026 college football season will likely be his last. College football players must be three years removed from high school before declaring for the NFL draft.

An Oct. 7 mock draft from The Athletic 's Nick Baumgardner has the Miami Dolphins selecting Smith with the No. 1 pick despite their need for a quarterback.

"Quarterback obviously would be an option for the Dolphins in Round 1, as would a trade. But this idea shouldn't be ruled out. Smith is truly one of the best wide receiver prospects of the past 25 years – possibly beyond," Baumgardner wrote.

A mock draft from CBS Sports ' Ryan Wilson also put Smith at the top spot.

Wrote Wilson: "Smith is the best player in college football, and it may not be particularly close. And if the Dolphins feel like Malik Willis is a better option than any of the QBs in this class, Smith is an easy choice here."

The Dolphins are a top candidate to land the No. 1 pick. They released veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa and wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and traded wide receiver Jaylen Waddle to the Denver Broncos for multiple draft picks. They are winless this season.

The Dolphins also signed Willis to a three-year, $67.5 million contract with $45 million guaranteed. Willis, a former third-round draft pick, played well as the Green Bay Packers' backup to Jordan Love. In two games as the starter last season, he threw for 409 yards and three touchdowns without an interception while rushing for 104 yards and two touchdowns.

MORE BUCKEYE, LESS AI: Prefer The Dispatch on Google

Despite giving Willis a lucrative deal, there's a chance the Dolphins could still go with a quarterback in the top spot. A mock draft from Sports Illustrated 's Justin Melo has Texas quarterback Arch Manning landing with the Dolphins, with Smith landing with the Titans at the No. 2 pick.

If Smith were drafted by the Titans, he would reunite with fellow Buckeyes receiver Carnell Tate, who was selected fourth in this year's draft. A year before that, the Titans selected Miami quarterback Cam Ward with the No. 1 pick.

"Yes, the Titans drafted Carnell Tate last year, but Smith is a near-perfect prospect who would give Ward an even better chance to reach his ceiling," Melo wrote.

Smith and Tate were a dynamic duo during the Buckeyes 2025 season. Smith finished with 1,243 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns last season, while Tate had 875 yards and nine touchdowns.

articles.title: How TC Taylor's play-calling improved Jackson State offense vs Mississippi Valley State
articles.summary: Jackson State football had one of its best offensive performances in SWAC play in its 38-7 win against Mississippi Valley State on Nov. 7.
articles.body:
To Jackson State football coach T.C. Taylor , it didn't matter that his team had 17 points and a 10-point lead at halftime.

To him, the Tigers were sleepwalking in the first half after scoring on three of their seven first-half drives.

"Like I've been having to tell them all year, 'Quit letting teams hang around,'" Taylor said of his message at halftime. "When we make our mind up to play, I don't think it's a team out there … that can stay with us."

This spurred JSU (7-2, 4-2 SWAC) to a 21-point second half in its 38-7 win over Mississippi Valley State (3-7, 2-4) at Mississippi Veterans Memorial Stadium on Nov. 7. The Tigers' 418 yards of total offense were their most since their loss to Grambling State on Oct. 10.

Jackson State football vs Mississippi Valley State, see top photos of SWAC game

The big change offensively was more involvement by Taylor in play-calling, which is normally handled by co-offensive coordinator Rip Kirk. Taylor said this was his first time calling plays in nearly two years, having not done so in 2025. JSU put up a scoring performance that ranks tied for first for the Tigers in SWAC play.

"It's something that I've always done in the past," Taylor said. "And anytime you've got this type of talent … it makes my job easy. But I've just got to shake off the rust and just, again, get these guys in position to make plays. … I like having fun. When we're having success, that's fun each and every time we're out there."

Taylor did also mention third-down conversions as the lone negative takeaway, adding that JSU has "got to be better in that aspect of the game" after going 3-for-11.

The JSU offense woke up on the second drive of the third quarter. Tight end Jency Riley Jr. caught a pass on a hitch route and turned it into an 81-yard touchdown on the lone play of the drive.

"Like Coach T.C. said, coming out of halftime, he was like, 'Don't sleepwalk,'" Riley said. "So, we had the play call, I caught it, seen grass, and therefore it was a foot race, and I don't think nobody can catch me in a straight line."

Riley's long touchdown was one of eight explosive plays the Tigers had that went for at least 15 yards, which Taylor was "proud of."

Riley finished as the team's leading receiver with 95 yards on four receptions with the one touchdown. He was one of three Tigers to catch a touchdown pass.

Quarterback Jared Lockhart threw for 299 yards, the most he's had in a SWAC game, on 22-for-33 completions with three passing touchdowns, an interception and a rushing touchdown.

Receiver Joanes Fortilien, who also caught a touchdown, finished with 81 yards on five receptions. Despite the offense's recent struggles, he didn't feel like the altered play-calling was something that was needed to unlock the Tigers' offense due to its personnel.

"I feel like our offense is powerful in every aspect," Fortilien said. "Everybody can do it. Shoot, you've just got to put the ball in the air, and we're going to come down with it."

articles.body:
TROY, Ala. (AP) — Marcus Calwise Jr. caught nine passes for 137 yards and a touchdown and Alonzo Jackson Jr. had a 66-yard scoop-and-score with 1:05 to go to cap off Louisiana Tech's 41-17 rout of Troy on Saturday.

The Bulldogs (7-2, 5-0 Sun Belt Conference) scored on each of their first three drives and four of their first five for a 20-10 halftime lead.

Kaegan Kent made field goals of 28 and 45 yards, Calwise had a 28-yard receiving score, and Sergio Snider punched it in from the 7 to pull away.

The Bulldogs held Troy (4-5, 2-3) to just seven points the rest of the way and forced three turnovers, including a strip-sack by Kolbe Fields that led to Jackson's fumble recovery touchdown.

Troy pulled within three points early in the third quarter following a strip-sack of Blake Baker that was recovered in the end zone.

Jackson paced the defense with 11 total tackles, two sacks, and 2 1/2 tackles for a loss.

Baker and Trey Kukuk split time at quarterback, each throwing for one touchdown.

Tucker Kilcrease threw for 215 yards for Troy. He lost two of Troy's five fumbles.

Louisiana Tech: hosts Southern Miss next Saturday.

articles.title: Florida State interim coach Rick Stockstill leads Seminoles to win in debut, ends road losing streak
articles.summary: Amari Thomas scored the go-ahead touchdown with 2:29 left as Florida State rallied from a 17-7 deficit to beat Boston College in Rick Stockstill's debut.
articles.body: Florida State opened the Rick Stockstill era with a road win Saturday. Those victories have been hard to come by for the Seminoles in recent years. FSU defeated Boston College 31-24 behind two rushing touchdowns from Amari Thomas. His 11-yard score late in the fourth quarter put the Seminoles ahead and made Stockstill a winner in his first game as interim coach. Entering Saturday, FSU had not won a game away from Doak Campbell Stadium since Nov. 25, 2023. Ashton Daniels completed 15 of 26 passes for 178 yards and an interception. Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie finished the day with 166 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception. ARCH MANNING, TEXAS ESCAPE MISSOURI AFTER WILD OFFICIATING CONTROVERSY SENDS SEC SHOWDOWN INTO CHAOS With it tied at 24-all, the Seminoles marched 90 yards in 14 plays, with Thomas breaking to the outside for the go-ahead score with 2:29 left. "This was emotional for me today," said a teary-eyed Stockstill, who was one of legendary FSU coach Bobby Bowden’s first quarterbacks. "I guess I wanted it as much for our players in there as I did for my former teammates and all our other players that came before us. It was special, it’s emotional. FLORIDA STATE FIRES AD MICHAEL ALFORD, AS MIKE NORVELL’S SEAT REACHES A BOILING POINT IN TALLAHASSEE "I poured my heart and soul into this place as a player, and I was going to do that for these next couple of months here," he said. McKenzie was shaken up and left midway into the third quarter, but returned the next series and capped off a crazy trick play when everyone on offense spun around in a circle before they lined up in a spread formation, snapped it and he tossed an underhanded pass for a two-yard touchdown to Javarius Green that pushed BC ahead 24-21. "It was just a play in our game plan that we thought would be good for these guys," BC coach Bill O’Brien said. Gabe Panikowski’s 22-yard field goal tied it. Playing its first game since firing coach Mike Norvell after six-plus seasons, Florida State erased a 17-7 second-quarter deficit by putting up two touchdowns in the final six minutes of the half. Thomas’ 20-yard run down the right sideline sliced the gap to three points. articles.title: Matt Rhule says Nebraska was due for 'a change' after coaching staff shakeup following loss to Illinois
articles.summary: Matt Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen just five days after calling him one of the best offensive minds, as Nebraska scored only 54 points in four losses.
articles.body: Nebraska coach Matt Rhule wants to see the Cornhuskers’ offense move in a different direction. The fourth-year Nebraska head coach removed Dana Holgorsen from his role as offensive coordinator, a move that was confirmed shortly after the Cornhuskers’ 24-13 loss to Illinois on Friday. The shakeup comes five days after Rhule called Holgorsen "one of the best offensive minds of our generation." Co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Glenn Thomas will take over play-calling duties for the Huskers, who have scored just 54 points while dropping four straight games. "Like so many of you, I am angry, I am disappointed and I am frustrated with our results this season," Rhule said in a statement. "As the head coach, I am ultimately responsible for every aspect of our program — including wins and losses — and it is my responsibility to make changes when they are warranted." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Rhule added that while he still respects Holgorsen’s coaching ability and leadership, the team's offense had reached a point where he believed change was necessary. "While there are many areas that need improvement, our offensive plan and execution is simply not working. Earlier today, I relieved offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen of his duties. As I have recently shared, Dana has a fantastic offensive mind, he is a strong leader, and he has done great work here at Nebraska. But simply, we need a change." OHIO STATE'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF HOPES TAKE BIG HIT WITH LOSS TO OREGON, JEREMIAH SMITH SHOWS FRUSTRATION Holgorsen was widely criticized for abandoning the running game and having quarterback Anthony Colandrea attempt 44 passes in a 17-10 loss to Washington. "Dana Holgorsen is one of the best offensive minds of our generation," Rhule said earlier this week. The Huskers were again plagued by penalties, missed field goals and questionable play-calling in the loss to Illinois. Nebraska scored on just two of its nine possessions against the Illini. Over the last four games, the Huskers have scored on nine of 46 possessions. "I will continue to evaluate our program through the season and certainly at its conclusion and make additional changes where I believe they will help us win," Rhule said. "The Nebraska fan base has high expectations and I embrace them, and I also know of their passionate support of the young men in our program. I hope they will continue to be there for our players with very important games still ahead. Our entire program is determined to finish this season strong." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Holgorsen was in his second full season as Nebraska’s offensive coordinator. He left his role as an offensive consultant at TCU in November 2024 to join the Cornhuskers in the same capacity, then was promoted to offensive coordinator a week later after Rhule moved Marcus Satterfield to another role. Nebraska travels to New Jersey next week for a matchup with Rutgers. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Out of 10 offensive drives for the Wildcats, three ended on punts, two on turnovers on downs, two on fumbles and one on an interception, as they only managed two field goals in the contest. articles.summary: Georgia's clock-eating rushing attack and Gunner Stockton's three touchdown passes overwhelmed Ole Miss as the Bulldogs silenced Trinidad Chambliss.

Ole Miss fans’ frustration boiled over after officials called pass interference against the Rebels with just over five minutes left in the second quarter. Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss did not throw a touchdown and was intercepted once. An 8-yard run by Ole Miss running back Shekai Mills-Knight with just under 11 minutes remaining finally put the Rebels on the board and cut Georgia’s lead to 35-7. OLE MISS DEFENSE TAKES CHARGE, SHUTS DOWN MISSOURI'S HIGH-POWERED RUSHING ATTACK IN 31-3 WIN Since 2023, no two SEC programs had posted better records than Georgia and Ole Miss.
