articles.title: Pumas and America tie in lively “Deja Vu” match
articles.summary: Pumas and America tied with 2 -2 score., a result that felt short for what each team needed
articles.body:
Pumas and America battled to a 2-2 tie in an exciting match that ended with result that doesn't benefit either side. It was a strange match that had very similar goals and which had end to end action and even a giant scuffle between teams. Pumas is basically out of the Liguilla with the result but will still hope to be able to get the miracle as they close out their season at home against Monterrey, while America will try to get back the first place spot in Liga MX that they lost on Saturday when they travel north to face off against struggling Tigres.

The 1st half started with both teams coming out with close to their best. While America was missing their best player in Brian Rodriguez, a solid player like Alejandro Zendejas was taking his place. A great run by Oscar Perea would end with him getting off a cross that Alejandro Zendejas would dive to head it past Pumas' goalkeeper, Keylor Navas to score the very early goal that gave America the 1-0 lead. It was a great start for America as Perea made a great play and Zendejas got off a great header. Pumas will respond almost immediately as Uriel Antuna would copy Perea and get past a defender and get off a cross into the area where Cesar Huerta would volley it past America's goalkeeper, Luis Malagon to score and tie the match at 1-1. It was a great play for the home side as Pumas now had tied the match which a very similar play to the goal scored by America. Off a counter, Huerta would get off a pass that turned into a shot that Malagon would clear with a kick. A cross into the area would fall to Adalberto Carrasquilla, whose shot would be deflected just wide. A huge scuffle between both teams after a foul by Kevin Alvarez on Huerta would end with a number of yellow cards to both sides. A cross into the area was wonderfully lowered by Perea but his right footed shot would go past Navas but also would go wide. Off a counter, Erick Sanchez got off a left footed shot from outside the area that went wide. A pass to Alvarez, would forced Navas to clear the ball just inside the area and the ball would be dangerous but it was cleared before Zendejas could lob it to the empty net. A cross into the area was bobbled by Malagon after he crashed into a player and the ball would fall to Robert Morales, who got off a right footed shot into the empty net to score. The goal would be called of in a controversial way after Referee Cesar Ramos ruled Nathan to be offside in the play where Malagon crashed into his teammate, Alan Cervantes. Once again Perea did a great job lowering the ball but his pass was cleared by Pumas' defense before Henry Martin could get to the empty net chance. The halftime whistle blew and both side had fought hard but the match remained tied.

The 2nd half started with neither team making a substitution yet. A counter would end up with Antuna having a wide open chance in the area but his lobbed shot was terrible and he was saved that the play would eventually be called offside. A cross into the area would eventually fall to Morales, who got off a bicycle kick that went horribly wide. A great counter ended with a great pass by Carrasquilla that found Juninho, who got off a terrible right footed shot that went well wide. A cross into the area was volleyed wide by Perea. America subbed out Carlos Alvarez for Miguel Borja. A great thru pass found a wide open Zendejas, who got off a bad left footed shot that went wide. Pumas subbed out Rodrigo Lopez and Juninho for Victor Arteaga and Alvaro Angulo. A cross into the area was volleyed wide from close range by Borja. A great combination play ended with Martin being brought down by Pablo Bennevendo in the area and the referee gave a Penalty Kick. Henry Martin stepped up to take the PK and got off a right footed shot past Navas to score and give America the 2-1 lead. America subbed out Alejandro Zendejas and Oscar Perea for Isaias Violante and Derek Jimenez. A minute after the play, off a free kick, Nathan would be brought down in the area by Ramos Mingo and a Penalty Kick was given to Pumas. Robert Morales stepped up to take the PK and got off a right footed shot past Malagon to score and tie the match at 2-2. In an incredible coincidence, just like in the first goal, Pumas had immediately copied America and scored in the same way. Pumas subbed out Uriel Antuna for Alan Medina. Violante got the ball in the area but his right footed shot was deflected wide. Off a free kick, Carrasquilla tried to surprise by taking a shot that went wide. Pumas tried a trick play off a free kick but Pedro Vite's left footed shot went wide. America subbed out Erick Sanchez and Kevin Alvarez for Edwin Cerrillo and Dagoberto Espinoza. Pumas subbed out Pedro Vite for Luciano Herrera. Cerrillo got off a right footed shot from outside the area that went well wide. Huerta got off a right footed shot that Malagon had a little trouble with it but eventually held on to the ball. The game was finishing with end to end action from both sides but few chances in the final third. In the end neither team will have a final chance and the match ended in a lively but strange 2-2 match.

Pumas and America battled in another edition of the Clasico Capitalino that ended with a tie that hurt both teams in the end. America had lost their first place lead after Cruz Azul defeated Tigres and leaped over them. The tie now means that another Cruz Azul victory will force America to end in second place. Yet it's much worse for Pumas who now needs to get a victory in their final match against Monterrey and for a couple of results to go their way to grab that final spot for the Liguilla. To make things worse, Pumas will need to do so without Pedro Vite who will be suspended because of Yellow cards. Pumas will host Monterrey at home while America travels to face off against Tigres.

articles.title: Too many mistakes bury UNLV as comeback bid against Wyoming falls short
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS—Just like that, the margin for error for the UNLV Rebels has officially hit zero.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS—Just like that, the margin for error for the UNLV Rebels has officially hit zero.

On Saturday, the Rebels were unable to crawl out of an early deficit, falling short of an incredible comeback in a 41-35 loss to Wyoming at Allegiant Stadium.

The loss officially means UNLV is no longer in control of its own destiny in regards to the Mountain West championship game, and a loss to New Mexico next week would likely all but eliminate the Rebels from contention.

"Obviously, extremely disappointed in our performance tonight," said UNLV head coach Dan Mullen.

"We got a lot of issues, a lot of things we got to fix."

There were many culprits for the loss, but one of the major sticking points was UNLV being unable to stop the run.

For the third straight week, the Rebels defense allowed the opponent to run the ball at will, with Wyoming putting up 351 net rushing yards. Running backs Samuel Harris and Markelle Holman each ran for over 100 yards, and quarterback Tyler Hughes ran for 71 yards on 12 carries before exiting the game due to injury before the end of the first half.

With over a thousand rushing yards given up over the last three games, stopping the run has gone from a sore spot to a genuine Achilles heel, and teams are now finding success with regularity on the ground.

"I got to look at us schematically, personnel-wise, who we have on the field and how we're doing coaching," said Mullen on the struggles in shoring up the run defense. "It's my job to fix it because it's not very good."

Offensive execution was not at its cleanest point either, putting UNLV behind the eight-ball early.

While Jackson Arnold did put together a couple of key plays with two touchdowns, he was wildly inefficient with a 7-for-18 passing line for 83 yards and an interception on a tipped ball. Jai'Den Thomas was having a relatively quiet day outside of an early touchdown, while the offensive line took a beating with four sacks in the first half, three of them from Wyoming linebacker Ethan Stuhlsatz.

In the third quarter, when Arnold was still struggling to move the ball down the field, Mullen decided to make the change and put Alex Orji in at quarterback.

"We just needed a spark," said Mullen on making the quarterback change.

"We just look lethargic out there on the field, and I was trying to look for a spark within the team."

From that point forward, something appeared to click offensively, as the Rebels were able to get the rushing attack figured out. Thomas would finish the day with 96 yards and two touchdowns on the night, while Orji would also put a touchdown on the board to put UNLV in a one-possession game with just under six minutes remaining.

However, the offense would ultimately commit the final mistake out of the two-minute warning, as the Rebels decided to pass and Orji ultimately threw a final interception that would allow Wyoming to ice the game.

"We were moving the ball right down the field right there," said Mullen as he explained the decision to go back to the passing attack despite the success in running the ball.

"On the first down play, they zero blitzed us. We had a guy on misprotection, and we had a guy wide open for the touchdown in the end zone on the first down play…second down, he was trying to make a play. I'll see it."

With the season looking more like it will finish below expectations, Mullen and UNLV now must have important decisions.

The Rebels should ultimately earn their way into bowl eligibility with three more chances to pick up their sixth win. However, the inconsistencies have put offensive coordinator Corey Dennis and defensive coordinator Paul Guenther on the hot seat late into the year.

"I look at everything within our program," Mullen said about making changes in the coaching staff.

"I look at whether it's our routine, whether it's what we do in preparing for today…I got to evaluate everything right there from play call to execution."

Whatever the Rebels' fate may be this season, the final three or four games of 2026 may require certain members of the staff to prove themselves.

articles.title: Liam Lawson's First F1 Podium Within Reach As Penalties Promote Him to Third for Sunday's Brazilian GP

Liam Lawson is in a strong position to secure his maiden Formula 1 podium at the Brazilian GP on Sunday at Interlagos. Lawson finds himself in this position after being promoted to P3 on the starting grid following penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

The Racing Bulls driver initially qualified fifth but will now line up on the second row, alongside Nico Hulkenberg , giving him an opportunity to fight for his first top-three finish on Sunday. It would be a significant milestone for Lawson, who is yet to secure a podium finish in his F1 career.

His P3 starting position also equals his career-best qualifying result, previously achieved at the 2025 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. His best Grand Prix result is fifth, which he has managed to score twice in Azerbaijan in 2025 and Monaco in 2026.

Meanwhile, Lando Norris secured his third consecutive pole at Interlagos after posting a 1:27.470 lap in a rain-soaked, heavily delayed qualifying session. The newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli will also start on the front row.

Liam Lawson Reflects on His Performance in Rain-Affected Qualifying

Despite securing a strong qualifying position, the 24-year-old driver admitted that he could have potentially challenged for an even better starting position.

After the Saturday session, when asked whether a front-row start was possible, Lawson acknowledged that it was difficult to predict, particularly with rain affecting the qualifying session. He posted the fifth-fastest lap time of 1:28.321 in wet conditions.

"I mean, as a driver, I'm going to say yes, but obviously you never know," Lawson said. "And obviously the rain was coming down. So by the time I got to the end of the lap… You never know.

"I don't know when everybody else did it. But, yeah, considering we got one lap, I think we did a good job."

Liam Lawson Optimistic About His Chances in Brazil

Despite thinking he left something on the table in terms of pace, the New Zealander was pleased with his qualifying performance and said: "It's still a good place to start. Obviously, I always take the free positions, but you always want to maximise as a driver as well."

Starting P3 puts Lawson in a strong position to challenge for his first F1 podium. However, Sunday's Brazilian GP could present several challenges, particularly given the rainy/overcast weather conditions expected at Interlagos.

Lawson, however, believes his Racing Bulls car has the pace to remain competitive regardless of the conditions.

"I think either way it's going to be a tough race here. I think it's unlikely it's going to be fully dry. But I think we have a quick car in all conditions," the 24-year-old said.

Liam Lawson, who is competing in his second full-time season with Racing Bull, is yet to secure a contract extension for next season. Therefore, a podium finish and consistently strong results in the remaining races of the season could strengthen his case for retaining his seat with the team in 2027.

articles.title: Texas college football rankings: Upon replay review, Texas Tech stays No. 1 ahead of Texas
articles.summary: The Red Raiders won an old-fashioned Big 12 shootout with defense to stay ahead of Texas, which scored a complete win over Missouri.
articles.body:
Texas Tech won a wild one, Texas showed some toughness, and UH survived as all three kept their CFP hopes alive for one more week.

The Chronicle's rankings for the 13 FBS teams in Texas:

An old-fashioned Big 12 game broke out in Lubbock, but it was three sacks in a row by the Red Raiders defense to wrap up a 53-48 win over West Virginia . The CFP may not like Tech's schedule, but we like the wins.

Upon replay review, this Texas team showed a lot in a 34-20 win at Missouri . We're going to wait and see how the Longhorns fare in Baton Rouge. We've been fooled before.

The Cougars' signature SLAB car had some engine troubles, and Houston may have sputtered at times itself but Willie Fritz will take the 31-24 win over Cincinnati. Also, offered without comment: former UH coach Dana Holgorsen was fired at Nebraska where he was offensive coordinator.

Maybe we were too harsh on the Mustangs after their loss at Syracuse. They looked just fine in a 51-28 win over Virginia Tech but will still need help to get to ACC title game.

It may be up to North Texas to make the American's bid for a CFP spot. The Mean Green are alone in first after beating Rice 52-23 and face UTSA next. They still would have to pass Boise State in the rankings.

Who needs Lincoln Riley or Jeff Traylor when you have Joe Klanderman? The interim coach is 2-0 after a 42-31 win over Iowa State. It helps to have a healthy DJ Lagway, too. Oh yeah, the Bears are bowl eligible.

The Aggies looked better at times but had to settle for too many field goals in a 17-9 loss at South Carolina . A&M will need to find two wins in final three games vs. Tennessee, at Oklahoma and vs. Texas to get a bowl bid.

Giving up 60 points and losing to FAU is no way for UTSA to make a case for the CFP's spot for a Group of 6 team.

TCU was on the verge of upsetting No. 24 Arizona but couldn't handle an onside pooch kick that led to the winning field goal. "It's been a frustrating year," coach Sonny Dykes said after the 29-28 loss.

The Bobcats fared much better in this week's Pac 12 After Dark. Of course, Oregon State isn't at quite the same level as Boise State.

The Owls have lost 11 in a row to FBS teams after falling at North Texas .

UTEP had a chance in the fourth quarter but 17-14 was as close as the Miners could get in a loss to Hawaii.

The Bearkats weren't any better after firing coach Phil Longo in a 47-14 loss to Jacksonville State.

articles.title: Hossam Hassan sacked as Egypt head coach over ex-wife scandal
articles.summary: A series of controversies surrounding Hassan’s marital life left a ‘negative impact’ on the team, Egyptian FA says.
articles.body:
The Egyptian Football Association (EFA) has dismissed national team coach Hossam Hassan, citing concerns over the image and stability of the national side after a series of controversies surrounding his marital life.

The EFA said on Saturday that it had reviewed recent events and their “negative impact on the positive image and stability” of the national team before deciding to part company with Hassan and his coaching staff, adding that “maintaining stability of the team is top priority”.

Ali Maher, currently in charge of club side Ceramica Cleopatra, was appointed his successor.

The move came three days after Egypt’s Supreme Council for Media Regulation banned Hassan from appearing on media platforms over a case linked to his private life and former wife.

Local media reported lawyers representing Hassan had filed a complaint against his ex-wife, Dina Mostafa, known publicly as “Dan Adam”, alleging forgery of official documents and bigamy.

Those allegations were denied by her representatives.

On the pitch, a 0-0 home draw with Angola in a Nations Cup qualifier in September came under scrutiny after Hassan substituted talisman Mohamed Salah in the 60th minute.

The Trabzonspor forward left the national team camp, and the EFA said he avoids playing on artificial pitches and, therefore, would miss the qualifier against South Sudan that same month, which Egypt won 5-0.

Hassan’s future had already been under scrutiny following a string of disputes after Egypt’s run to the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup, the country’s best-ever performance at the tournament.

The former striker, who took charge in March 2024, also led Egypt to the semifinals of the Africa Cup of Nations before a fourth-place finish.

Hassan, who received a three-match ban from FIFA after criticising the referee following Egypt’s knockout World Cup defeat by Argentina, left the national team after 38 matches in charge, winning 21, drawing 10 and losing seven.

Former Egypt attacker Mido said in September the situation had “gone out of control” and called for officials to intervene.

Maher, 52, will take charge before Egypt’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Malawi on November 13 and 17.

articles.title: Cincinnati provides update on JV Gibson injury
articles.summary: Gibson was alert and moving all extremities after a scary injury. He traveled back to Cincinnati with the team.
articles.body:
With roughly seven minutes remaining in a heated Big 12 showdown between Cincinnati and Houston, the atmopshere inside TDECU Stadium abruptly changed. The crowd fell silent, and the passion and energy inside the building quickly turned into concern.

Cincinnati wide receiver JV Gibson suffered a frightening collision with Houston strong safety Jordan Allen while running a post route toward the end zone. The impact left Cincinnati's leading receiver motionless on the field, prompting officials to throw flags for pass interference and targeting penalties.

But the officiating decisions quickly became secondary. As Gibson remained down with an apparent head injury, medical personnel rushed onto the field to attend the receiver. Members of the Cincinnati roster left the sideline to gathered around their teammate, kneeling nearby as trainers continued their evaluations. Gibson's parents eventually made their way to the field as well.

The game was delayed 16 minutes as medical personnel stabilized Gibson, placed him on a stretcher, and transported out of TDECU Stadium. His father accompanied him on the back of the medical cart. Gibson subsequently made his way to Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center. Before his departure, Cincinnati Athletics reported the receiver as "alert and moving all extremities."

"Our personnel did an amazing job to get out there very quickly, they were right on top of JV," Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield said in the immediate aftermath of the game. "Ultimately, they got him in a good place there. He was moving all four extremities on command. They took him to the hospital for precautionary reasons, and obviously they got to do their CT scans and those type of things. I don't have an update, but hopefully everything checks out great. I thought JV was playing awesome tonight and unfortunately that happened to him. Prayers go out to JV and his family, but it's a blessing for him to move all four extremities. It's always very scary, and scary for our team."

In a later update, Cincinnati's official Twitter account confirmed that Gibson had been discharged from Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center and traveled back to Cincinnati with the team.

articles.title: Oklahoma QB John Mateer sends powerful message after win over Florida
articles.summary: John Mateer expressed a unity message about the Oklahoma Sooners’ chemistry and bond following their 23-7 win over the Florida Gators on Saturday evening. Ma...
articles.body:
John Mateer expressed a unity message about the Oklahoma Sooners' chemistry and bond following their 23-7 win over the Florida Gators on Saturday evening.

Mateer is going through the senior campaign of his collegiate career with the Sooners. While the team has gone through mixed results, the quarterback has persevered to be productive on the field.

For this game, Mateer shined with a big performance on the road. He completed 21 out of 33 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 14 times for 56 yards. The quarterback reflected on the victory after the game, having firm praise on how the team came together to pull off this win over Florida, who were ranked in the AP Top 25.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"We just believed something like this can happen, and kids like us can make a decision. But everybody in the building decided to fight and play for each other, and we started off with a good flow. Need to score more touchdowns. Field goals are cool, but we want touchdowns. But it was good, man. And we have each other's back, and that matters," Mateer said on the ESPN broadcast.

"We knew coming in here it's a great environment. We were saying in the locker, this is what you dream of. As a kid, so many great players have played here, and we love each other like we're not going to give up on each other. Some people might quit. Some people might want us to quit because the trials are hard, and they are. But we give it to God, and we do it for each other."

Mateer and Oklahoma controlled the game from start to finish. They did an excellent job containing Florida's attack, only conceding a touchdown in the second quarter.

Rocky Beers led receivers with four catches for 72 yards. Isaiah Sategna III came next with four receptions for 34 yards and a touchdown, while Hayden Hansen caught a three-yard touchdown pass.

The Sooners will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14.

articles.title: Khawaja denies throwing ‘anyone under the bus’ over Sandpapergate scandal
articles.summary: Australian cricketer defends waiting so long to place blame, denying it was a marketing ploy to sell his book.
articles.body:
Usman Khawaja has denied he has “thrown anyone under the bus” a day after the former Australian cricketer released an excerpt from his autobiography claiming the entire team had been aware of ball-tampering during a 2018 tour of South Africa.

The scandal – called Sandpapergate over Australia’s scuffing of the ball with sandpaper during the March 2018 Test in Cape Town – sparked a major integrity crisis for Cricket Australia.

Captain Steve Smith and batsmen David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with the sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their part in the scandal.

In a video posted on Instagram on Sunday, Khawaja said he had wanted to “come clean” about the incident since 2018.

“I haven’t thrown anyone under the bus,” added the 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket in January.

“The guys currently in the team and the other people who were there on the South African tour, including me, we’re not the victims.

“These three guys [Bancroft, Warner and Smith] took the blame for all of us, and they’re the victims.”

Khawaja said he had spoken with the three players and promised Warner he would share his side of the story.

“These three guys deserve justice, and I haven’t pointed fingers at anyone,” he added.

“I’m still searching for what I was searching all those years ago: For us – me included – to take the blame together as a team so we can all move on from this once and for all.”

Khawaja, who retired after 88 Tests, defended waiting so long to make the claims, denying it was a marketing ploy to sell his book.

He said he wanted to go public in 2018 once Smith, Warner and Bancroft were suspended.

“But Smudge [Smith] being the man and leader he was, he talked me out of it.

“He wanted to take the blame. I argued with him, but he was having none of it. That’s the first time I tried to come out.”

Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.

But after extensive talks with then-coach Justin Langer, he decided not to, he said.

Khawaja said he never felt comfortable talking after that while back in the Australian team from 2022.

“Call me a chicken or whatever you want. I didn’t know how to do it because I was still in the team,” Khawaja said. “I was always conscious of putting my team first, but I’m not in that team any more.”

Australia’s Test side returned to South Africa for the first time since 2018 last month and were beaten 2-1 by the hosts in the three-match series, which was overshadowed in part by discussions of the scandal and the upcoming release of Khawaja’s book.
